notes.title: Sparklite Out Now on Linux! Plus New Features + Fixes!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33695339/c1ff97ac14729b77f6741b582e719528edf08f59.png[/img]

We're delighted to announce the arrival of Sparklite on Linux! The whimsical action-adventure game released today and includes the latest content update for Sparklite!

Linux users will be delighted with this new release as well as the amount of content and new features it includes. 

Please find the full list of new features + fixes below:

[i][b]Features[/b][/i]
•	Added support for hot swapping between controllers on PC
•	Harmony’s finale is now worthy of the work that it takes to assemble her band. Collect all the beats to see it!
•	Added several forest rooms to improve general feel of the zone
•	Improvements to UX on Inventory screen:
	- Widgets now quick equip
	- Visual indicators for passive gadgets and widgets more clear
	- Gadgets dim when in equip mode
	- Tooltips revised
•	Controllers not on our official supported list should at least display button indicators now
•	Reworked Description panel in Inventory
	- Now requires a button press to get more info but cleans up the UI
•	Add music to Furnaces
•	Audio no longer ducks in Options from Main Menu
•	Added new “Plays Best with Controller” toast at start-up

[i][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/i]

[i][b]Critical[/b][/i]
•	Fixed occasional crash when spamming the talk button in Founder’s dialog
•	Fixed crash on Inventory Menu when pressing confirm without anything selected

[i][b]Medium[/b][/i]
•	Fixed mountains room ledge that people were getting stuck on
•	Fixed Golden Woods tile that was broken
•	Fixed mountains room pit that was too difficult
•	Remove invisible “No” button in Co-Op Menu Dialog
•	Mis-clicking anywhere in menus no longer removes focus of current selection
•	Fixed UI anchoring issues on 1920x1200
•	Prevent multiple menu options from being highlighted at the same time with mouse hovering
*	Desert boss body parts now hit-flash like the other bosses
*	Re-balance final boss fight to have more consistent enemies

[i][b]Low[/b][/i]
•	Removed some unclear room symbols Goldenwoods minimap 
•	Storm Weather effect now is a shader, partial fix for dark UI screens during storm
•	Wingnut no longer flies off-screen during chat cinematic
•	Typo in illumination patch
•	Fix visual glitch with nameplate when moving between objects (ex. Hawk and Hawk’s Dog)
•	Wrong sound played when equipping a Patch, now fixed
•	Credits no longer scrollable with mouse
•	1x2 Patches now display as Invalid in all expected cases
•	Muckvac no longer stays on without button held down
•	Fix visual glitch on title bar animations when interacting with objects. Title bar would freeze and not display during popup.
•	Brighten up final boss fight a bit visually

To find out more about Sparklite, head here: https://store.steampowered.com/app/943140/Sparklite/ or, join the [url=https://discord.gg/merge]Merge Games Discord server[/url].

Wanna chat with the devs? Stop by the [url=https://discord.gg/eWp5dTH]Sparklite Dev Discord Server[/url].

See you in Geodia!

notes.notes:
Hello Adventurers!

We hope you’re enjoying your adventures in Geodia!

We’re proud to announce the arrival of the biggest ever update for our whimsical action-adventure, [b]Sparklite[/b]!
Sparklite players will be delighted with the amount of extra content and new features we’ve managed to cram into this latest update. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33695339/3c171889ea53127f0f3ed778df6e1deb2c389ab5.png[/img]

Sparklite players who install [b]Update 1.5[/b] can look forward to; 
[list]
[*] New! [b]Casual Game Mode[/b] - For an easier experience
[*] New! [b]Champion Game Mode[/b] - For the hardcore gamer looking to challenge themselves
[*] Updated save slot UI
[*] Enhanced boss fights
[*] New character in the Refuge
[*] New Baron cinematic
[*] Updated sinkholes
[*] Updated Furnaces
[*] Chopping grass now has a chance to drop Sparklite
[*] Thanks to active community we’ve also added lots of bug fixes and quality of life improvements 
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33695339/9aac3c180e72608af5854cf98a0370b3235ce1a9.png[/img]

[h1]Casual Game Mode:[/h1]
The brand-new [b]Casual Game Mode[/b] is intended for people who mostly just want to see everything Sparklite has to offer, without the pressure of failure. In this mode, hearts drop more often, players begin their adventure with more health & there are also more dig spots. This mode is ideally suited to players who want to focus on Sparklite’s story and enjoy the world of Geodia.

[h1]Champion Game Mode:[/h1]
For players who like an additional challenge after beating the game. Ada's adventure will be harder this time around. Enemies and Titans will be stronger and have new attacks but, the rewards will be greater as they will drop more Sparklite. Players start the game with all schematics but Vaults no longer appear in the world. Choose this mode for a whole new way to experience Sparklite!

Finally, as if that wasn’t enough, you can now also earn unique banners in Town, (which can be seen on all saves, not just the one you finished the game on), for beating Standard and Champion modes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33695339/0606b899506e5e2ca748f2c2833ccf8a0f823bfd.gif[/img]
We also made the following changes in other updates: 
[h1]Winter update – Dec 19[/h1]
[list]
[*] End Run option from Pause Menu (Player Request)
[*] Show Beat Counts on World Map - all beats available for each area in a given run
[*] Add more space for available patches
[*] Minor audio improvements
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33695339/4ab031540eb04abdfdf4062b52ae37a7235542f1.gif[/img]

[h1]January update – Jan 10 [/h1]
[list]
[*] Added an Adventure Log, which shows stats per run
[*] Added Patch scroll menu
[*] Added saving the game when changing scenes
[*] Added winter effects in town
[*] Added NPC names to Interact prompt
[*] Improved art of core sequence
[*] Rework beats to spawn more often
[*] Added “Quick Equip" and "Quick Unequip" prompts in Patch Menu
[*] Improved audio for Scubert fight
[/list]

We hope all of these improvements / additions help you to have even more fun in Sparklite, until next time…gear up for adventure!

Thanks again to our [b]Sparklite Community[/b] for your ongoing support and dedicated feedback

See you in Geodia!

notes.title: Sparklite is a roguelike which runs on FOMO
notes.notes:
On the surface, Sparklite is as generically, pleasantly roguelikelike as it’s possible to get. You wander around randomly generated areas, clubbing baddies with a wrench and spelunking in sinkholes for treasure, before taking on big gits in caves. The story is bland as weetabix, there are secrets to be found everywhere, and there are helpful items that give you new abilities. The game is pretty good. But the thing that made it stand out for me – the thing that made it different – is the way it teased me with shiny new gadgets, and then snatched them away from me.

notes.title: Sparklite Titan Tactics - Boris
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33695339/9e2d7707dc55a2c35411cd68444ba570c200ef39.png[/img]

Hello, and welcome to [b]Titan Tactics[/b], an in-depth look at the villainous henchmen working for the evil [b]Baron[/b] in [b]Sparklite[/b], the retro-inspired action adventure coming to PC, Nintendo Switch, Xbox One & PlayStation 4 on November 14th! Today, we'll be talking about [b]Boris[/b], the menacing miner who will pulverize any boulder, or anyone, in his way.
 
[b]Boris[/b], with the help of his rock-devouring [b]wrecking ball[/b], has become one of the Baron’s top miners. He’s been tasked with trying to enter the [b]Foothills Vault[/b] but, to the Baron’s great disappointment, has so far been unable to break the seal. You could say he’s caught between a rock and a hard place…

A keen scavenger, Boris was born to dig. His latest project, before siding with the nefarious Baron on his quest to drain [b]Geodia[/b] of its natural resources, was helping archaeologists search for [b]Founder’s relics[/b] in the [b]Shifting Sands[/b], a noble enough cause if ever there was one.
 
However, eventually he became disgruntled by all the ‘do-gooders’ wanting to protect Geodia and the wildlife found within it. He thought all that nonsense just got in the way of unleashing the relics’ dormant (yet potentially catastrophic) powers, and that the destruction of the land’s natural resources was a small price to pay for this! When the Baron offered him a job leading a crew of gremilns in the mines, he didn’t hesitate and soon got to work…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33695339/b54157f9b717643e53fb43c4cbd07e104499338b.png[/img]
 
When you ([b]Ada[/b]), meet Boris, watch out for his [b]vacuum[/b]! After pulverizing nearby boulders, The Boring Titan uses the [b]Sparklite Combustor’s[/b] heat to produce an incredibly strong vacuum. The vacuum sucks up any uncrushed rubble into the titan’s core where it will then be ground to dust. Only objects able to run directly away from the force of the vacuum can avoid the Titan’s clutches. Keep an eye out for his vacuum, and flee as soon as you see it!

That’s all for today’s edition of [b]Titan Tactics[/b], come back next week when we’ll place the spotlight on another one of the [b]Baron’s Titans[/b], and tell you what you need to know to stand a chance when you take them on…

notes.title: Sparklite Preview; Purifying the World With Science - via TechRaptor
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33695339/50c833024423b651a299f3188c80bb0d6193b67e.gif[/img]

'Recently I met with [Kevin Mabie of Red Blue Games] to talk about Sparklite and take a look at a demo. The story follows a female engineer named Ada who has to save the world of Geodia by taking down the evil Baron. Sparklite powers everything in Geodia and if harnessed safely, it doesn’t leave a negative impact. However, that leads to our villain, the Baron, polluting the world by aggressively mining and burning Sparklite for power.

"[...] we really wanted to confront greed as a whole—especially when it disregards the effects/damage it causes to everyone else and the environment,” Mabie said about the villain’s motivation. “The villain in Sparklite, the Baron, is inspired from the robber barons following the industrial revolution era, often characterized as in pursuit of wealth and power.”

After crashlanding on Geodia, Ada runs into corrupted Gremlins and creatures tarnished by the Baron’s greed. Equipped with a wrench, she collects Sparklite passively to upgrade her gear and fuel a floating town known as The Refuge. This is where NPCs take Ada to after falling in battle. 

The demo immediately presents me with a way to upgrade my wrench into a multi-tool through the use of patches. Attaching those to a Patch Board on Ada’s wrench increases her health, damage, and energy used for special abilities. The special abilities function as Gadgets in Sparklite, tying into Red Blue Games’ focus on science.'

notes.title: Meet Pogo!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33695339/e9d31e10660c85292237af282b24c28c11175840.gif[/img]

We want all of our characters in Sparklite to have personality and charm. Our artist Rafael Françoi ([url=https://twitter.com/rathaelos]@rathaelos[/url]) has created a bunch of great “spice idle” animations (not seen in this video) for many of our NPCs to give them a bit more personality. Of course we wish we could do even more animations but we need to stay focused on more significant features. I’m sure every indie struggles with this but it’s always hard to say “good enough” and move on, even when you know you could do so much more.

Margo and Pogo are two of the NPCs you’ll find along your journey in Sparklite. Eager to see the world, yet overconfident in their abilities, they frequently find themselves lost and separated from one another. It will be up to you to reunite them whenever they get split up. If a Fracture happens before finding them both, though, they’ll get split up all over again. In return for your help you’ll get rewards like patches that will upgrade your stats.

notes.title: We now have a 🍉juicy, 🎞️tweeny, ⚙️geary Pause Menu!
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33695339/906fabcf8938cb760f45203611c978f28347cb05.gif[/img]

It’s Lucas (designer/programmer) here to show off the 4th-wall-breaking Pause Menu. Maybe it’s my background in web development but I love a solid, usable, juicy UI. Our process on this Pause Menu feature could be fun to see and was kind of textbook design and implementation so I thought I’d share a bit about it for all the gamedevs out there.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/943140/Sparklite/

We were working with an outside programmer-friend and both of our artists on this, so we wanted requirements to be pretty solid to avoid miscommunication between the team. To do that, we created wireframes in Figma, which is mostly a tool for mobile app prototypes and website interface design. But it worked really well at creating a clickable wireframe. I actually even use Figma for some simple game design “paper” prototypes.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33695339/3a586edb66dab63cdbbe4b7b6613180037dc4f8a.gif[/img]

In the video above you can see we referenced Hyper Light Drifter for the audio meters. We are big believers in using references to find out how other people have tackled similar problems and understand UI design patterns. So, once we had the wireframes set up in Figma, Rafael did a rough mockup of a style we could use. 

Then once we approved it, he filled out and added tweens, and finally, art that our programmer could import and reference when implementing UI tweening.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33695339/8c6d6ba552004816c42395cd95fe1edd59feffff.gif[/img]

I’m sure our programmer could talk about all the little hurdles along the way, (including that custom font) but we can save that for another post. We are super happy with how our team worked together to produce this UI and we think it turned out great.

Here's a short dev-diary on how we do effects in #sparklite. 

Our effects can be pure spritesheet animations, particle systems, or any combination of the two. We chose this approach because particle systems can add a lot of world feel by accounting for things like gravity and velocity in a way that pure animation usually can't. At the same time, there are occasions when the charm of a hand-made pixel animation is needed. Getting particle systems to look harmonious with our pixel-art style is a bit challenging, but with some self-restraint and meticulousness it's doable. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/943140/Sparklite/

An effect be in any of the following states (among other sub-states).

- Spawn
- Idle (looping or not)
- Die

They can also trigger rumble, fire off other effects when they die, and play sounds. It's a fairly robust system that does about 80% of what we need it to.

notes.title: Jump down!
notes.notes:
Allowing the player to move in 3D space within 2D art is extremely difficult. Early on we did a lot of experimentation to decide between using 3D physics or faked 3D physics. Both have their limitations, creating optical illusions where either gameplay doesn't match the visual representation or vice versa.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33695339/7377c4fb9dfc15d791b46a7bbc629dc5c73d1265.gif[/img]

Tall objects, for example, are problematic because as they get taller their collision needs to reach other heights. In this screenshot, the tall vine object actually would want to have a collider at each height we support. If we used 3D space instead, we could just provide a 3D collider and be done.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33695339/ba75f74b0fbf015cecce19225573cac0490bd0fb.png[/img]

Making the object appear more top-down helps clean the collision up, but removes some of the character of the sprite. Given that Unity has made a lot of 2D tiling improvements since we began development, we might do it differently if we were to start over tomorrow.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33695339/def310692fffd86643447a102ee4a7584fc87392.gif[/img]

Feel free to reach out and ask questions if you're interested in learning more about our approach. We always like to share our solutions but don't want to go too far into the weeds with everyone.

notes.title: Welcome to Sparklite
notes.notes:
Welcome intrepid Steam user,

Please let us take this opportunity to welcome you to the world of Sparklite - We are Red Blue Games, a small indie studio based out of North Carolina. We plan to post regular updates to this Steam community hub so bookmark us and stay in touch. To begin with here’s a little background info about our team; Ed, Lucas and Kevin.

Co-founders Edward and Lucas began making games to share with one another. From Mario levels drawn on spools of printer paper to Lego-based RPGs, their many experiments instilled a love of game making from an early age. Similarly, Kevin developed his passion for game making when he was young, drawing alternative Zelda screens when bored in school, and replaying the tune of his favourite game tracks on his toy piano at home. Together, they've now turned their passion for game creation into Red Blue Games, where they make game experiences to share with the world, Sparklite being the first.
